question: Does explicitly starting Video Talk and granting browser camera permission authorize model-triggered one-frame captures for the active session when a persistent local preview is visible and frames go directly to OpenAI?
rationale: The code can enforce same-origin access and browser-direct delivery, but maintainers must choose the acceptable user-consent boundary for model-triggered camera capture.

options.title: Approve session-scoped consent
options.body: Treat Video Talk activation, native browser permission, and a persistent preview as sufficient authorization for bounded captures during that session.

options.title: Require capture-time indication
options.body: Add a conspicuous visual indication or confirmation whenever `describe_view` captures and sends a frame.

options.title: Pause camera delivery
options.body: Keep audio Talk unchanged and defer frame delivery until a stricter camera-consent design is approved.

recommendation.title: Approve session-scoped consent
recommendation.body: Treat Video Talk activation, native browser permission, and a persistent preview as sufficient authorization for bounded captures during that session.
